sanskrit: tathā sarveṇa sainyena rājā duryodhanas tadā drauṇer anantaraṃ prāyāt sodaryaiḥ parivāritaḥ
english: Then King Duryodhana, with his whole host, advanced just behind the son of Droṇa, ringed about by his own brothers.

sanskrit: duryodhanād anu kṛpas tataḥ śāradvato yayau evam eṣa mahāvyūhaḥ prayayau sāgaropamaḥ
english: After Duryodhana came Kṛpa, the son of Śaradvat; and thus this great battle-array set forth, vast as the ocean.

sanskrit: rejus tatra patākāś ca śvetacchatrāṇi cābhibho aṅgadāny atha citrāṇi mahārhāṇi dhanūṃṣi ca
english: There, O lord, shone the banners and the white parasols, the bright armlets, and the precious, beautifully wrought bows.

sanskrit: taṃ tu dṛṣṭvā mahāvyūhaṃ tāvakānāṃ mahārathaḥ yudhiṣṭhiro 'bravīt tūrṇaṃ pārṣataṃ pṛtanāpatim
english: Beholding that great array of your men, the mighty chariot-warrior Yudhiṣṭhira spoke at once to the son of Pṛṣata, the commander of his host:

sanskrit: paśya vyūhaṃ maheṣvāsa nirmitaṃ sāgaropamam prativyūhaṃ tvam api hi kuru pārṣata māciram
english: "Behold, O great archer, the array they have fashioned, vast as the sea. Do you too, O son of Pṛṣata, form a counter-array without delay."

sanskrit: tataḥ sa pārṣataḥ śūro vyūhaṃ cakre sudāruṇam śṛṅgāṭakaṃ mahārāja paravyūhavināśanam
english: Then the brave son of Pṛṣata, O great king, formed a most fearsome array, the Śṛṅgāṭaka, which could shatter the enemy's formation.

sanskrit: śṛṅgebhyo bhīmasenaś ca sātyakiś ca mahārathaḥ rathair anekasāhasrais tathā hayapadātibhiḥ
english: At its horns stood Bhīmasena and the great chariot-warrior Sātyaki, with chariots in their many thousands and with horse and foot.

sanskrit: nābhyām abhūn naraśreṣṭhaḥ śvetāśvo vānaradhvajaḥ madhye yudhiṣṭhiro rājā mādrīputrau ca pāṇḍavau
english: At its center stood that best of men, white-horsed, ape-bannered Arjuna; and in the midst were King Yudhiṣṭhira and the two Pāṇḍava sons of Mādrī.

sanskrit: athetare maheṣvāsāḥ sahasainyā narādhipāḥ vyūhaṃ taṃ pūrayām āsur vyūhaśāstraviśāradāḥ
english: And the other great archers, the lords of men with their forces, skilled in the science of battle-arrays, filled out that formation.

sanskrit: abhimanyus tataḥ paścād virāṭaś ca mahārathaḥ draupadeyāś ca saṃhṛṣṭā rākṣasaś ca ghaṭotkacaḥ
english: Behind them came Abhimanyu, and the great chariot-warrior Virāṭa, and the exultant sons of Draupadī, and the Rākṣasa Ghaṭotkaca.

sanskrit: evam etaṃ mahāvyūhaṃ vyūhya bhārata pāṇḍavāḥ atiṣṭhan samare śūrā yoddhukāmā jayaiṣiṇaḥ
english: Having drawn up this great array, O Bhārata, the valiant Pāṇḍavas stood ready for battle, eager to fight and longing for victory.

sanskrit: bherīśabdāś ca tumulā vimiśrāḥ śaṅkhanisvanaiḥ kṣveḍitāsphoṭitotkruṣṭaiḥ subhīmāḥ sarvatodiśam
english: The tumultuous beat of drums, mingled with the blare of conch-shells and the roars, the slapping of arms, and the war-cries, grew terrible on every side.

sanskrit: tataḥ śūrāḥ samāsādya samare te parasparam netrair animiṣai rājann avaikṣanta prakopitāḥ
english: Then the warriors, closing upon one another in the fray, O king, glared at each other with unblinking eyes, kindled with fury.

sanskrit: manobhis te manuṣyendra pūrvaṃ yodhāḥ parasparam yuddhāya samavartanta samāhūyetaretaram
english: First in their minds, O lord of men, those warriors set themselves against one another for battle, challenging each man his fellow.

sanskrit: tataḥ pravavṛte yuddhaṃ ghorarūpaṃ bhayāvaham tāvakānāṃ pareṣāṃ ca nighnatām itaretaram
english: Then there broke out a battle dreadful to look upon and full of terror, as your men and the foe struck down one another.

sanskrit: nārācā niśitāḥ saṃkhye saṃpatanti sma bhārata vyāttānanā bhayakarā uragā iva saṃghaśaḥ
english: Sharp iron shafts fell in the fray, O Bhārata, terror-bringing with their gaping mouths, like serpents in swarms.

sanskrit: niṣpetur vimalāḥ śaktyas tailadhautāḥ sutejanāḥ ambudebhyo yathā rājan bhrājamānāḥ śatahradāḥ
english: Bright spears flew forth, oil-washed and keenly whetted, blazing like lightning-flashes leaping from the clouds, O king.

sanskrit: gadāś ca vimalaiḥ paṭṭaiḥ pinaddhāḥ svarṇabhūṣitāḥ patantyas tatra dṛśyante giriśṛṅgopamāḥ śubhāḥ nistriṃśāś ca vyarājanta vimalāmbarasaṃnibhāḥ
english: And maces wrapped in bright cloth and adorned with gold were seen falling there, fair as mountain-peaks; and the swords gleamed, resembling the clear sky.

sanskrit: ārṣabhāṇi ca carmāṇi śatacandrāṇi bhārata aśobhanta raṇe rājan patamānāni sarvaśaḥ
english: And shields of bull's hide, marked with a hundred moons, O Bhārata, shone splendidly in the battle, O king, as they fell on every side.

sanskrit: te 'nyonyaṃ samare sene yudhyamāne narādhipa aśobhetāṃ yathā daityadevasene samudyate abhyadravanta samare te 'nyonyaṃ vai samantataḥ
english: The two armies, contending with one another in the fray, O lord of men, shone like the hosts of the Daityas and the gods arisen for war; and they rushed upon each other on every side in the battle.

sanskrit: rathās tu rathibhis tūrṇaṃ preṣitāḥ paramāhave yugair yugāni saṃśliṣya yuyudhuḥ pārthivarṣabhāḥ
english: Chariots, swiftly driven by their warriors in that fierce encounter, locked yoke against yoke; and those bulls among kings fought on.

sanskrit: dantināṃ yudhyamānānāṃ saṃgharṣāt pāvako 'bhavat danteṣu bharataśreṣṭha sadhūmaḥ sarvatodiśam
english: From the clashing of the battling tuskers, O best of the Bhāratas, fire arose upon their tusks, with smoke, on every side.

sanskrit: prāsair abhihatāḥ ke cid gajayodhāḥ samantataḥ patamānāḥ sma dṛśyante giriśṛṅgān nagā iva
english: Some of the elephant-warriors, struck through by lances on all sides, were seen falling like trees tumbling from a mountain-peak.

sanskrit: pādātāś cāpy adṛśyanta nighnanto hi parasparam citrarūpadharāḥ śūrā nakharaprāsayodhinaḥ
english: And foot-soldiers too were seen striking one another down, brave men of varied aspect, fighting with claw-blades and lances.

sanskrit: anyonyaṃ te samāsādya kurupāṇḍavasainikāḥ śastrair nānāvidhair ghorai raṇe ninyur yamakṣayam
english: Closing upon one another, the soldiers of the Kurus and the Pāṇḍavas sent each other, with dreadful weapons of every kind, to the abode of Yama.

sanskrit: tataḥ śāṃtanavo bhīṣmo rathaghoṣeṇa nādayan abhyāgamad raṇe pāṇḍūn dhanuḥśabdena mohayan
english: Then Bhīṣma, son of Śāntanu, making all resound with the rumble of his chariot, came upon the Pāṇḍavas in the fray, bewildering them with the twang of his bow.

sanskrit: pāṇḍavānāṃ rathāś cāpi nadanto bhairavasvanam abhyadravanta saṃyattā dhṛṣṭadyumnapurogamāḥ
english: And the chariots of the Pāṇḍavas too, roaring with a fearsome din, rushed forward girt for battle, with Dhṛṣṭadyumna at their head.

sanskrit: tataḥ pravavṛte yuddhaṃ tava teṣāṃ ca bhārata narāśvarathanāgānāṃ vyatiṣaktaṃ parasparam
english: Then the battle broke out between your men and theirs, O Bhārata, with men, horses, chariots, and elephants entangled one with another.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca bhīṣmaṃ tu samare kruddhaṃ pratapantaṃ samantataḥ na śekuḥ pāṇḍavā draṣṭuṃ tapantam iva bhāskaram
english: Saṃjaya said: Bhīṣma, wrathful in the battle and scorching all around, the Pāṇḍavas could not bear to look upon, as upon the blazing sun.

sanskrit: tataḥ sarvāṇi sainyāni dharmaputrasya śāsanāt abhyadravanta gāṅgeyaṃ mardayantaṃ śitaiḥ śaraiḥ
english: Then, at the command of the son of Dharma, all the troops rushed upon the son of Gaṅgā, who was crushing them with his sharp arrows.

sanskrit: sa tu bhīṣmo raṇaślāghī somakān sahasṛñjayān pāñcālāṃś ca maheṣvāsān pātayām āsa sāyakaiḥ
english: But that Bhīṣma, glorying in battle, struck down with his shafts the Somakas together with the Sṛñjayas and the great-archer Pāñcālas.

sanskrit: te vadhyamānā bhīṣmeṇa pāñcālāḥ somakaiḥ saha bhīṣmam evābhyayus tūrṇaṃ tyaktvā mṛtyukṛtaṃ bhayam
english: Cut down by Bhīṣma, the Pāñcālas together with the Somakas charged swiftly at Bhīṣma himself, casting aside the fear that death inspires.

sanskrit: sa teṣāṃ rathināṃ vīro bhīṣmaḥ śāṃtanavo yudhi ciccheda sahasā rājan bāhūn atha śirāṃsi ca
english: Then the hero Bhīṣma, son of Śāntanu, severed in an instant, O king, the arms and heads of those chariot-warriors in the fight.

sanskrit: virathān rathinaś cakre pitā devavratas tava patitāny uttamāṅgāni hayebhyo hayasādinām
english: Your father Devavrata stripped the chariot-warriors of their cars; and the heads of the horsemen fell from their steeds.

sanskrit: nirmanuṣyāṃś ca mātaṅgāñ śayānān parvatopamān apaśyāma mahārāja bhīṣmāstreṇa pramohitān
english: And we saw elephants, emptied of their riders and lying like hills, O great king, stupefied by Bhīṣma's weapon.

sanskrit: na tatrāsīt pumān kaś cit pāṇḍavānāṃ viśāṃ pate anyatra rathināṃ śreṣṭhād bhīmasenān mahābalāt
english: There was not one man among the Pāṇḍavas there, O lord of peoples, save the foremost of chariot-warriors, the mighty Bhīmasena.

sanskrit: sa hi bhīṣmaṃ samāsādya tāḍayām āsa saṃyuge tato niṣṭānako ghoro bhīṣmabhīmasamāgame
english: For he, closing with Bhīṣma, smote him in the fray; and then a dreadful crash arose at the meeting of Bhīṣma and Bhīma.

sanskrit: babhūva sarvasainyānāṃ ghorarūpo bhayānakaḥ tathaiva pāṇḍavā hṛṣṭāḥ siṃhanādam athānadan
english: Terrible and fearsome it was to all the troops; and so the Pāṇḍavas, rejoicing, raised then a lion's roar.

sanskrit: tato duryodhano rājā sodaryaiḥ parivāritaḥ bhīṣmaṃ jugopa samare vartamāne janakṣaye
english: Then King Duryodhana, ringed about by his brothers, guarded Bhīṣma in the battle while the slaughter of men went on.

sanskrit: bhīmas tu sārathiṃ hatvā bhīṣmasya rathināṃ varaḥ vidrutāśve rathe tasmin dravamāṇe samantataḥ sunābhasya śareṇāśu śiraś ciccheda cārihā
english: But Bhīma, that best of chariot-warriors, having slain Bhīṣma's charioteer, while the horses of the car bolted and it careered on every side, that slayer of foes swiftly severed with a shaft the head of Sunābha.

sanskrit: kṣurapreṇa sutīkṣṇena sa hato nyapatad bhuvi hate tasmin mahārāja tava putre mahārathe nāmṛṣyanta raṇe śūrāḥ sodaryāḥ sapta saṃyuge
english: By that keen razor-edged arrow he was slain and fell to the earth; and when that son of yours, the great chariot-warrior, was slain, O great king, his seven valiant brothers could not endure it in the fight.

sanskrit: ādityaketur bahvāśī kuṇḍadhāro mahodaraḥ aparājitaḥ paṇḍitako viśālākṣaḥ sudurjayaḥ
english: Ādityaketu, Bahvāśin, Kuṇḍadhāra, Mahodara, Aparājita, Paṇḍitaka, Viśālākṣa, and Sudurjaya —

sanskrit: pāṇḍavaṃ citrasaṃnāhā vicitrakavacadhvajāḥ abhyadravanta saṃgrāme yoddhukāmārimardanāḥ
english: in gleaming harness, with their varied armor and standards, those crushers of foes, eager to fight, rushed upon the Pāṇḍava in the battle.

sanskrit: mahodaras tu samare bhīmaṃ vivyādha patribhiḥ navabhir vajrasaṃkāśair namuciṃ vṛtrahā yathā
english: Mahodara pierced Bhīma in the fray with nine feathered shafts like thunderbolts, as the slayer of Vṛtra pierced Namuci.

sanskrit: ādityaketuḥ saptatyā bahvāśī cāpi pañcabhiḥ navatyā kuṇḍadhāras tu viśālākṣaś ca saptabhiḥ
english: Ādityaketu struck him with seventy, Bahvāśin with five, Kuṇḍadhāra with ninety, and Viśālākṣa with seven.

sanskrit: aparājito mahārāja parājiṣṇur mahārathaḥ śarair bahubhir ānarchad bhīmasenaṃ mahābalam
english: Aparājita, O great king, the ever-victorious great chariot-warrior, assailed the mighty Bhīmasena with many arrows.

sanskrit: raṇe paṇḍitakaś cainaṃ tribhir bāṇaiḥ samardayat sa tan na mamṛṣe bhīmaḥ śatrubhir vadham āhave
english: And Paṇḍitaka in the fray struck at him with three arrows. But Bhīma could not endure this assault from his foes in the battle.

sanskrit: dhanuḥ prapīḍya vāmena kareṇāmitrakarśanaḥ śiraś ciccheda samare śareṇa nataparvaṇā
english: Gripping his bow with his left hand, that tormentor of foes severed in the fray, with a smooth-jointed arrow, the head

sanskrit: aparājitasya sunasaṃ tava putrasya saṃyuge parājitasya bhīmena nipapāta śiro mahīm
english: of your son Aparājita, with its handsome nose; and overcome by Bhīma in the fight, his head fell to the earth.

sanskrit: athāpareṇa bhallena kuṇḍadhāraṃ mahāratham prāhiṇon mṛtyulokāya sarvalokasya paśyataḥ
english: Then with another broad-headed shaft he dispatched the great chariot-warrior Kuṇḍadhāra to the world of the dead, before the eyes of all.

sanskrit: tataḥ punar ameyātmā prasaṃdhāya śilīmukham preṣayām āsa samare paṇḍitaṃ prati bhārata
english: Then once more the warrior of measureless soul, fitting an arrow to the string, sent it in the battle against Paṇḍita, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: sa śaraḥ paṇḍitaṃ hatvā viveśa dharaṇītalam yathā naraṃ nihatyāśu bhujagaḥ kālacoditaḥ
english: That shaft, having slain Paṇḍita, entered the surface of the earth, as a serpent, driven by fate, swiftly enters it after striking a man dead.

sanskrit: viśālākṣaśiraś chittvā pātayām āsa bhūtale tribhiḥ śarair adīnātmā smaran kleśaṃ purātanam
english: Cleaving off the head of Viśālākṣa with three arrows, the undaunted hero felled it to the ground, remembering an old grievance.

sanskrit: mahodaraṃ maheṣvāsaṃ nārācena stanāntare vivyādha samare rājan sa hato nyapatad bhuvi
english: He pierced the great archer Mahodara through the breast with an iron shaft in the fray, O king; and slain, he fell to the earth.

sanskrit: ādityaketoḥ ketuṃ ca chittvā bāṇena saṃyuge bhallena bhṛśatīkṣṇena śiraś ciccheda cārihā
english: And having shorn away the standard of Ādityaketu with a shaft in the fight, that slayer of foes severed his head with a most keen broad-headed arrow.

sanskrit: bahvāśinaṃ tato bhīmaḥ śareṇa nataparvaṇā preṣayām āsa saṃkruddho yamasya sadanaṃ prati
english: Then Bhīma, in great wrath, sent Bahvāśin with a smooth-jointed arrow to the abode of Yama.

sanskrit: pradudruvus tatas te 'nye putrās tava viśāṃ pate manyamānā hi tat satyaṃ sabhāyāṃ tasya bhāṣitam
english: Then the others, your remaining sons, fled away, O lord of peoples, deeming true that which he had spoken in the assembly-hall.

sanskrit: tato duryodhano rājā bhrātṛvyasanakarśitaḥ abravīt tāvakān yodhān bhīmo 'yaṃ yudhi vadhyatām
english: Then King Duryodhana, stricken by the calamity of his brothers, said to your warriors: "Let this Bhīma be slain in the battle!"

sanskrit: evam ete maheṣvāsāḥ putrās tava viśāṃ pate bhrātṝn saṃdṛśya nihatān prāsmaraṃs te hi tad vacaḥ
english: Thus those great-archer sons of yours, O lord of peoples, seeing their brothers slain, called to mind that vow of his.

sanskrit: yad uktavān mahāprājñaḥ kṣattā hitam anāmayam tad idaṃ samanuprāptaṃ vacanaṃ divyadarśinaḥ
english: What the deeply wise Vidura had spoken, salutary and unerring — that word of the seer with divine vision had now come to pass.

sanskrit: lobhamohasamāviṣṭaḥ putraprītyā janādhipa na budhyase purā yat tat tathyam uktaṃ vaco mahat
english: Possessed by greed and delusion, through love of your sons, O lord of men, you did not heed in time that great and truthful word.

sanskrit: tathaiva hi vadhārthāya putrāṇāṃ pāṇḍavo balī nūnaṃ jāto mahābāhur yathā hanti sma kauravān
english: Surely it is for the destruction of your sons that the mighty, strong-armed Pāṇḍava was born, even as he now slaughters the Kauravas.

sanskrit: tato duryodhano rājā bhīṣmam āsādya māriṣa duḥkhena mahatāviṣṭo vilalāpātikarśitaḥ
english: Then King Duryodhana, O honored sir, approaching Bhīṣma, overcome by great grief and utterly worn, lamented thus:

sanskrit: nihatā bhrātaraḥ śūrā bhīmasenena me yudhi yatamānās tathānye 'pi hanyante sarvasainikāḥ
english: "My valiant brothers have been slain by Bhīmasena in the battle, and the rest, though they strive their utmost, are being slain along with all my soldiers."

sanskrit: bhavāṃś ca madhyasthatayā nityam asmān upekṣate so 'haṃ kāpatham ārūḍhaḥ paśya daivam idaṃ mama
english: "And you, in your neutrality, ever disregard us. I have set my foot upon an evil road — behold this fate of mine!"

sanskrit: etac chrutvā vacaḥ krūraṃ pitā devavratas tava duryodhanam idaṃ vākyam abravīt sāśrulocanam
english: Hearing this cruel speech, your father Devavrata spoke this word to Duryodhana, whose eyes were filled with tears:

sanskrit: uktam etan mayā pūrvaṃ droṇena vidureṇa ca gāndhāryā ca yaśasvinyā tattvaṃ tāta na buddhavān
english: "This was told you before by me, and by Droṇa and by Vidura, and by the illustrious Gāndhārī — the truth, my child, which you did not understand."

sanskrit: samayaś ca mayā pūrvaṃ kṛto vaḥ śatrukarśana nāhaṃ yudhi vimoktavyo nāpy ācāryaḥ kathaṃ cana
english: "And an agreement was made by me with you before, O scourge of foes: that neither I nor the preceptor are ever to be relieved of duty in battle."

sanskrit: yaṃ yaṃ hi dhārtarāṣṭrāṇāṃ bhīmo drakṣyati saṃyuge haniṣyati raṇe taṃ taṃ satyam etad bravīmi te
english: "For whichever of the sons of Dhṛtarāṣṭra Bhīma shall set eyes upon in the fray, him will he slay in the battle — this I tell you truly."

sanskrit: sa tvaṃ rājan sthiro bhūtvā dṛḍhāṃ kṛtvā raṇe matim yodhayasva raṇe pārthān svargaṃ kṛtvā parāyaṇam
english: "Therefore, O king, grow firm, and fixing your resolve steadfastly upon the fight, do battle with the Pārthas, making heaven your final goal."

sanskrit: na śakyāḥ pāṇḍavā jetuṃ sendrair api surāsuraiḥ tasmād yuddhe matiṃ kṛtvā sthirāṃ yudhyasva bhārata
english: "The Pāṇḍavas cannot be conquered, not even by the gods and demons with Indra at their head. Therefore, fixing your mind firmly upon the battle, fight on, O Bhārata."

sanskrit: dhṛtarāṣṭra uvāca dṛṣṭvā mama hatān putrān bahūn ekena saṃjaya bhīṣmo droṇaḥ kṛpaś caiva kim akurvata saṃyuge
english: Dhṛtarāṣṭra said: When they saw my many sons slain by one man, O Saṃjaya, what did Bhīṣma, Droṇa, and Kṛpa do in the battle?

sanskrit: ahany ahani me putrāḥ kṣayaṃ gacchanti saṃjaya manye 'haṃ sarvathā sūta daivenopahatā bhṛśam
english: Day after day my sons go to their destruction, O Saṃjaya. I think, O charioteer, that they are altogether and grievously smitten by fate.

sanskrit: yatra me tanayāḥ sarve jīyante na jayanty uta yatra bhīṣmasya droṇasya kṛpasya ca mahātmanaḥ
english: Since all my sons are vanquished and do not conquer — and that too in the presence of Bhīṣma, of Droṇa, and of the great-souled Kṛpa,

sanskrit: saumadatteś ca vīrasya bhagadattasya cobhayoḥ aśvatthāmnas tathā tāta śūrāṇāṃ sumahātmanām
english: and of the heroic son of Somadatta, and of both Bhagadatta and Aśvatthāman, my child — those most great-souled heroes —

sanskrit: anyeṣāṃ caiva vīrāṇāṃ madhyagās tanayā mama yad ahanyanta saṃgrāme kim anyad bhāgadheyataḥ
english: and of the other heroes — that my sons, standing in their very midst, should be slain in the battle, what can this be but the working of destiny?

sanskrit: na hi duryodhano mandaḥ purā proktam abudhyata vāryamāṇo mayā tāta bhīṣmeṇa vidureṇa ca
english: For the dull-witted Duryodhana would not understand what was foretold of old, though he was restrained by me, my child, and by Bhīṣma and Vidura,

sanskrit: gāndhāryā caiva durmedhāḥ satataṃ hitakāmyayā nāvabudhyat purā mohāt tasya prāptam idaṃ phalam
english: and by Gāndhārī too — that witless one — ever out of desire for his good. He did not heed it of old, through delusion; and this is the fruit that has come to him.

sanskrit: yad bhīmasenaḥ samare putrān mama vicetasaḥ ahany ahani saṃkruddho nayate yamasādanam
english: For Bhīmasena, enraged, day after day in the battle leads my senseless sons to the abode of Yama.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca idaṃ tat samanuprāptaṃ kṣattur vacanam uttamam na buddhavān asi vibho procyamānaṃ hitaṃ tadā
english: Saṃjaya said: This is the coming-to-pass of that excellent word of Vidura, which you did not understand, O lord, when it was spoken for your good in that hour.
